primitives.name: BrainDeformationModeling
primitives.verbatim_quote: We adopt a physics-based modeling approach, and describe the brain deformation in mechanical terms (such as displacements, strains and stresses), which can be computed using a biomechanical model, by solving a continuum mechanics problem.
primitives.assumptions: Continuum hypothesis, neglect microstructural effects, assume local equilibrium.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs at extreme strain rates or under catastrophic failure.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian updating of pre-operative imaging data with real-time intraoperative measurements.
layer2.telemetry: Residual error between predicted and observed brain shift vectors.

primitives.name: FiniteElementDiscretization
primitives.verbatim_quote: We discuss finite element and meshless domain discretization, the use of the Total Lagrangian formulation of continuum mechanics, and explicit time integration for solving both time-accurate and steady state problems.
primitives.assumptions: Spatial discretization error balances temporal truncation error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mesh tangling or particle disorder leads to numerical instability.

layer2.mapping: Conformal prediction intervals for uncertainty quantification in state estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Number of active elements/particles per unit volume.

primitives.name: ContactHandling
primitives.verbatim_quote: We present the methods developed for handling contacts and for warping 3D medical images using the results of our simulations.
primitives.assumptions: Coulomb friction law applies, contact stiffness much larger than bulk modulus.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of contact triggers non-smooth dynamics and solver divergence.

layer2.mapping: State-transition logic for detecting tool-tissue interactions in surgical robotics.
layer2.telemetry: Penetration depth and contact force history.

primitives.name: LargeDeformationAnalysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: From the point of view of solution methods, we advocate the use of fully nonlinear modeling approaches, capable of capturing very large deformations and nonlinear material behavior.
primitives.assumptions: Geometric nonlinearity dominates, linear elasticity fails.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Material incompressibility breaks down under extreme volumetric strain.

layer2.mapping: Unification of heterogeneous sensor data via Kalman filtering.
layer2.telemetry: Logarithmic strain measure exceeding threshold value.

primitives.name: Total_Lagrangian_Formulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We use the Total Lagrangian formulation [52], where all variables are referred to the initial (undeformed) configuration of the system.
primitives.assumptions: The undeformed initial configuration serves as a fixed reference frame; material properties are defined relative to this state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the initial configuration becomes invalid due to extreme deformation.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction via pre-computation of kernel matrices, enabling fast empirical risk minimization.
layer2.telemetry: Pre-computed stiffness matrices serve as verification metrics for real-time updates.

primitives.name: Explicit_Time_Integration
primitives.verbatim_quote: 3.2 Time integration The integration of continuum mechanics equations in the time domain can be performed using either implicit or explicit methods [53, 54].
primitives.assumptions: Time steps are conditionally stable, bounded by the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition related to material stiffness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Instability arises when the time step exceeds the critical CFL limit.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state-transition dynamics through discrete event scheduling, where actions trigger immediate state changes.
layer2.telemetry: Discrete event timestamps track the progression of state transitions.

primitives.name: Underintegrated_Hexahedron
primitives.verbatim_quote: However, implicit time integration methods require a set of nonlinear algebraic equations to be solved at each time step.
primitives.assumptions: Reduced integration prevents volumetric locking, sacrificing some accuracy for computational efficiency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rank deficiency occurs when the reduced integration fails to capture strain energy correctly.

layer2.mapping: Derives a lightweight predictive kernel for GSI inference, focusing on low-rank approximations of covariance matrices.
layer2.telemetry: Condition numbers of reduced-rank matrices serve as leakage diagnostics.

primitives.name: Volumetric_Locking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Furthermore, multiple iterations may be needed at each time step to control the error and prevent divergence.
primitives.assumptions: Incompressibility constraint leads to spurious pressure modes that inflate the stiffness matrix.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Locking occurs when the bulk modulus approaches infinity, rendering the element nearly inextensible.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE robust reasoning through constrained optimization, where hard constraints prevent certain state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Constraint satisfaction ratios measure the degree of locking in decision-making processes.

primitives.name: Diagonal Mass Lumping
primitives.verbatim_quote: When a diagonal (lumped) mass matrix is used, the discretized equations are decoupled.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear momentum balance and finite element spatial discretization; uses diagonal lumping to approximate the consistent mass matrix.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when material inertia becomes highly anisotropic or when high-frequency dynamic instabilities dominate, rendering the lumped approximation invalid.

layer2.mapping: Maps diagonal mass lumping to conformal prediction intervals in GSI, where the decoupling reduces computational complexity for real-time uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Computational wall-clock time per time step, which should remain constant regardless of mesh size for efficient scaling.

primitives.name: Explicit Time Integration
primitives.verbatim_quote: 5.1.4 Solution algorithm For the time integration of partial differential equations of equilibrium we used the explicit method described in Section 3 above.
primitives.assumptions: Relies on small enough time steps to satisfy the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) stability condition; assumes negligible implicit coupling between degrees of freedom.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the CFL condition becomes too restrictive, leading to excessive computational cost or numerical instability in stiff systems.

layer2.mapping: Maps explicit time stepping to online learning updates in GSE, where predictions are made sequentially without solving global equations, enabling fast situational reasoning.
layer2.telemetry: Maximum stable time step duration, which directly impacts the speed of state transitions in real-time applications.

primitives.name: Edge-Based Hausdorff Distance
primitives.verbatim_quote: Unlike most purely image-based registration methods, the application of the biomechanicsbased approach does not require any parameter tuning, and the results presented in the next Section demonstrate the predictive (rather than explanatory) power of this method.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that geometric edges are well-defined and that the distance metric captures the relevant misalignment between reference and deformed configurations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when noise corrupts edge detection, causing spurious correspondences or when the topology of the object changes significantly.

layer2.mapping: Maps edge-based Hausdorff to conformal prediction regions in GSI, where the distance serves as a verification metric for probabilistic brain shift maps.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of correctly aligned edges within a clinically acceptable threshold (e.g., 1.7 mm), reflecting registration accuracy.

primitives.name: Nonlocking Tetrahedral Elements
primitives.verbatim_quote: Brain tissue's incompressibility necessitates the use of nonlocking tetrahedral elements such as the one described in Joldes et al.
primitives.assumptions: Enforces volume conservation under affine deformation; mitigates volumetric locking through reduced integration or specialized shape functions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the mesh quality deteriorates (e.g., highly skewed elements) or when the material undergoes extreme compression/expansion beyond the assumed constitutive range.

layer2.mapping: Maps nonlocking elements to robust feature extraction in GSE, where the formulation handles distorted sensor data without introducing spurious constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Mesh distortion metrics (e.g., Jacobian determinant) that indicate element validity during continuous state estimation.

primitives.name: Image Registration Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: 28 image registration, utilization of hyperthreading features available in CPUs installed in many off-the-shelf personal desktop and laptop computers may provide sufficient computation speed.
primitives.assumptions: Computation speed scales with CPU hyperthreading; image registration is computationally feasible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When computational resources exceed real-time constraints for image alignment.

primitives.name: Computational Mechanics Medical Translation
primitives.verbatim_quote: One of the greatest challenges for the field of Computational Mechanics is to translate it's phenomenal success to medicine.
primitives.assumptions: Success in computational mechanics can be adapted to clinical applications.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When general-purpose computational frameworks fail to meet medical specificity requirements.

primitives.name: Personalized Medicine Computational Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Computational Mechanics can become a central enabling discipline contributing to the creation of a new era of personalized medicine based on patient-specific scientific computations.

primitives.name: Real-Time Surgical Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Computational efficiency is an important issue, as intraoperative applications, requiring reliable results within approximately 40 seconds, are most appealing.
primitives.assumptions: Intraoperative simulations must complete within strict temporal bounds.

These primitives enable accurate image registration and real-time simulation, essential for guiding neurosurgeons and training surgeons.
